_meta.indication: ZYNYZ is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC), under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 2, open-label, multiregional, multicenter, single-arm study; retifanlimab 500 mg Q4W IV
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced Merkel cell carcinoma who had not received prior systemic therapy for their advanced disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) assessed by independent central review according to RECIST v1.1
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 52% (34/65), 95% CI 40, 65; 12 (18%) complete responses; DOR ≥6 months for 76% and ≥12 months for 62% of responders

key_safety: Most common (≥10%) adverse reactions were fatigue (28%), musculoskeletal pain (22%), pruritus (18%), diarrhea (15%), rash (11%), pyrexia (10%), and nausea (10%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 22% of patients; most frequent (≥2%) were fatigue, arrhythmia, and pneumonitis. Includes immune-mediated adverse reactions.
target_moa: Retifanlimab is a humanized IgG4κ monoclonal antibody that recognizes and blocks PD-1 from interacting with its ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2, restoring T-cell effector function.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee discussion was held for this BLA application; FDA had approved two drugs in the same class based on single-arm trials and no new issues were identified.

description.text: Added Zynyz in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel for first-line SCAC and as a single agent for platinum-refractory locally recurrent/metastatic SCAC

citations.quote: - In combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel for the first-line treatment of adult patients with metastatic or with inoperable locally recurrent squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal (SCAC).

description.text: Converted accelerated approval to traditional approval for metastatic or recurrent locally advanced Merkel cell carcinoma

citations.quote: • updates the Zynyz (retifanlimab-dlwr) Prescribing Information with data from the Final Study Report of Study INCMGA 0012-201 entitled “A Phase 2 study of INCMGA00012 in Patients with Merkel Cell Carcinoma (POD1UM-201).” This Report was associated with postmarketing requirement (PMR) 4412-1 included in the March 22, 2023, approval letter.• supports the conversion of accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601 Subpart E of the metastatic or recurrent locally advanced Merkel cell carcinoma indication to traditional approval.

description.text: Added new dosing regimen of 375 mg every 3 weeks for the squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal (SCAC) indications

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sBLA provides for a new dosing regimen for Zynyz (retifanlimab-dlwr) injection, for intravenous use, of 375 mg every 3 weeks for the squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal (SCAC) indications.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Tumor response rate (ORR) and duration of response

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response.

The magnitude of the durable ORR is sufficient to serve as an endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit to patients, and is acceptable to support granting accelerated approval of retifanlimab for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced Merkel cell carcinoma.

confirmatory_requirement.text: PMR 4412-1: a multicenter clinical trial to confirm clinical benefit in patients with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced MCC not previously treated with systemic therapy, enrolling at least 100 patients followed for a minimum of 12 months.

citations.quote: 4412-1 Conduct a multicenter clinical trial intended to confirm the clinical benefit of retifanlimab-dlwr in patients with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) who have not received prior systemic therapies for metastatic or recurrent locally advanced MCC. The trial will enroll at least 100 patients to be followed for a minimum of 12 months to establish the objective response rate and characterize the durability of response. summary.text: BLA 761334 received priority review and was granted accelerated approval on March 22, 2023 based on ORR and duration of response from the single-arm PODIUM-201 study, with orphan drug designation for MCC and a required confirmatory postmarketing trial (PMR 4412-1) to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: This application (BLA 761334) was granted priority review because the other available immunotherapy options for the treatment of MCC remain under accelerated approval status.
It is approved under the provisions of accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 601.41), effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon approved labeling.
